name: elasticbeanstalk
description: AWS Elastic Beanstalk AWS Elastic Beanstalk makes it easy for you to create, deploy, and manage scalable, fault-tolerant applications running on the Amazon Web Services cloud.

subcommands.name: abort-environment-update
subcommands.description: Cancels in-progress environment configuration update or application version deployment.

subcommands.name: apply-environment-managed-action
subcommands.description: Applies a scheduled managed action immediately.

subcommands.name: associate-environment-operations-role
subcommands.description: Add or change the operations role used by an environment.

subcommands.name: check-dns-availability
subcommands.description: Checks if the specified CNAME is available.

subcommands.name: compose-environments
subcommands.description: Create or update a group of environments that each run a separate component of a single application.

subcommands.name: create-application
subcommands.description: Creates an application that has one configuration template named default and no application versions.

subcommands.name: create-application-version
subcommands.description: Creates an application version for the specified application.

subcommands.name: create-configuration-template
subcommands.description: Creates an AWS Elastic Beanstalk configuration template, associated with a specific Elastic Beanstalk application.

subcommands.name: create-environment
subcommands.description: Launches an AWS Elastic Beanstalk environment for the specified application using the specified configuration.

subcommands.name: create-platform-version
subcommands.description: Create a new version of your custom platform.

subcommands.name: create-storage-location
subcommands.description: Creates a bucket in Amazon S3 to store application versions, logs, and other files used by Elastic Beanstalk environments.

subcommands.name: delete-application
subcommands.description: Deletes the specified application along with all associated versions and configurations.

subcommands.name: delete-application-version
subcommands.description: Deletes the specified version from the specified application.

subcommands.name: delete-configuration-template
subcommands.description: Deletes the specified configuration template.

subcommands.name: delete-environment-configuration
subcommands.description: Deletes the draft configuration associated with the running environment.

subcommands.name: delete-platform-version
subcommands.description: Deletes the specified version of a custom platform.

subcommands.name: describe-account-attributes
subcommands.description: Returns attributes related to AWS Elastic Beanstalk that are associated with the calling AWS account.

subcommands.name: describe-application-versions
subcommands.description: Retrieve a list of application versions.

subcommands.name: describe-applications
subcommands.description: Returns the descriptions of existing applications.

subcommands.name: describe-configuration-options
subcommands.description: Describes the configuration options that are used in a particular configuration template or environment, or that a specified solution stack defines.

subcommands.name: describe-configuration-settings
subcommands.description: Returns a description of the settings for the specified configuration set, that is, either a configuration template or the configuration set associated with a running environment.

subcommands.name: describe-environment-health
subcommands.description: Returns information about the overall health of the specified environment.

subcommands.name: describe-environment-managed-action-history
subcommands.description: Lists an environment's completed and failed managed actions.

subcommands.name: describe-environment-managed-actions
subcommands.description: Lists an environment's upcoming and in-progress managed actions.

subcommands.name: describe-environment-resources
subcommands.description: Returns AWS resources for this environment.

subcommands.name: describe-environments
subcommands.description: Returns descriptions for existing environments.

subcommands.name: describe-events
subcommands.description: Returns list of event descriptions matching criteria up to the last 6 weeks.

subcommands.name: describe-instances-health
subcommands.description: Retrieves detailed information about the health of instances in your AWS Elastic Beanstalk.

subcommands.name: describe-platform-version
subcommands.description: Describes a platform version.

subcommands.name: disassociate-environment-operations-role
subcommands.description: Disassociate the operations role from an environment.

subcommands.name: list-available-solution-stacks
subcommands.description: Returns a list of the available solution stack names, with the public version first and then in reverse chronological order.

subcommands.name: list-platform-branches
subcommands.description: Lists the platform branches available for your account in an AWS Region.

subcommands.name: list-platform-versions
subcommands.description: Lists the platform versions available for your account in an AWS Region.

subcommands.name: list-tags-for-resource
subcommands.description: Return the tags applied to an AWS Elastic Beanstalk resource.

subcommands.name: rebuild-environment
subcommands.description: Deletes and recreates all of the AWS resources (for example: the Auto Scaling group, load balancer, etc.) for a specified environment and forces a restart.

subcommands.name: request-environment-info
subcommands.description: Initiates a request to compile the specified type of information of the deployed environment.

subcommands.name: restart-app-server
subcommands.description: Causes the environment to restart the application container server running on each Amazon EC2 instance.

subcommands.name: retrieve-environment-info
subcommands.description: Retrieves the compiled information from a RequestEnvironmentInfo request.

subcommands.name: swap-environment-cnames
subcommands.description: Swaps the CNAMEs of two environments.

subcommands.name: terminate-environment
subcommands.description: Terminates the specified environment.

subcommands.name: update-application
subcommands.description: Updates the specified application to have the specified properties.

subcommands.name: update-application-resource-lifecycle
subcommands.description: Modifies lifecycle settings for an application.

subcommands.name: update-application-version
subcommands.description: Updates the specified application version to have the specified properties.

subcommands.name: update-configuration-template
subcommands.description: Updates the specified configuration template to have the specified properties or configuration option values.

subcommands.name: update-environment
subcommands.description: Updates the environment description, deploys a new application version, updates the configuration settings to an entirely new configuration template, or updates select configuration option values in the running environment.

subcommands.name: update-tags-for-resource
subcommands.description: Update the list of tags applied to an AWS Elastic Beanstalk resource.

subcommands.name: validate-configuration-settings
subcommands.description: Takes a set of configuration settings and either a configuration template or environment, and determines whether those values are valid.

subcommands.name: wait
subcommands.description: Wait until a particular condition is satisfied.

subcommands.name: environment-exists
subcommands.description: Wait until JMESPath query Environments[].Status returns Ready for all elements when polling with ``describe-environments``.

subcommands.name: environment-terminated
subcommands.description: Wait until JMESPath query Environments[].Status returns Terminated for all elements when polling with ``describe-environments``.

subcommands.name: environment-updated
subcommands.description: Wait until JMESPath query Environments[].Status returns Ready for all elements when polling with ``describe-environments``.
